questions.q: Let $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=-3f(x+2)-4=-3(x+2)^2-4$. Find $g(0)$, and describe the transformation from $f$ to $g$ in words.
questions.answer: $g(0)=-3(2)^2-4=-3(4)-4=-16$. $g$ is $f$ shifted left $2$, reflected over the $x$-axis and stretched vertically by a factor of $3$, then shifted down $4$.

questions.q: Using the same $g(x)=-3(x+2)^2-4$, find $g(-2)$, and explain why this is the vertex of $g$'s graph.
questions.answer: $g(-2)=-3(0)^2-4=-4$. Since $f(x)=x^2$ has its vertex (minimum) at $x=0$, and $g$ shifts $f$ left by $2$, the transformed vertex sits at $x=-2$.

questions.q: Classify $f(x)=x^4+2x^2-5$ as even, odd, or neither.
questions.answer: Only even-degree terms appear ($x^4$, $x^2$, and the constant), so by Theorem 3.1 $f$ is even. Check: $f(2)=16+8-5=19$ and $f(-2)=16+8-5=19$ ✓.

questions.q: Classify $h(x)=2x^5-3x$ as even, odd, or neither.
questions.answer: Only odd-degree terms appear ($x^5$, $x$), so by Theorem 3.1 $h$ is odd. Check: $h(1)=2-3=-1$ and $h(-1)=-2+3=1=-h(1)$ ✓.

questions.q: Explain why $k(x)=x^2+x$ is neither even nor odd.
questions.answer: $k$ mixes an even-degree term ($x^2$) with an odd-degree term ($x$), so Theorem 3.1 doesn't apply to the whole function. Checking directly: $k(1)=2$ and $k(-1)=0$, which is neither equal to $k(1)$ (even) nor $-k(1)=-2$ (odd).
Need $x^2-25\neq0 \Rightarrow x\neq\pm5$. Domain: all reals except $5$ and $-5$.

questions.q: Let $p(x)=2x+3$ for $x<1$, and $p(x)=x^2-1$ for $x\geq1$. Find $p(-2)$ and $p(3)$.
questions.answer: Since $-2<1$, use the first piece: $p(-2)=2(-2)+3=-1$. Since $3\geq1$, use the second piece: $p(3)=3^2-1=8$.
